name: Lango
region: Lango sub-region, northern Uganda: Lira, Apac, Oyam, Kole, Dokolo, Alebtong, Otuke, Amolatar, Kwania
translator_note: Everyday Lira Lango, the way a young professional talks to a friend: 'Mak i UG' for Book, 'Go cim kwoŋo' for Call ahead, 'cente me cim' for mobile money, 'ka ame cunyi yom iye' (where your heart is at ease) for 'where you are comfortable'. Lango markers are used throughout rather than Acholi ones: kede (with), ame (that/which), a- adjectives (aber, adit, atek), kop (word/matter), pwod (still), kuca (there), boma (town), ateni (true), leb Munu (English), ŋ in poŋ, ŋeo, lwoŋ. The four verbs are Wot. Nywak. Pango. Ter. Product words with no settled Lango term (sandbox, plug-in, endpoint, API key, link, wallet, prototype) are loans or short paraphrases and are listed under uncertain; the verb 'riyo' for driving also needs a native check.
